title: Left derivability structure for a full subcategory
statement:
Let $A$ be a category [def-nagata-category] and $W$ a class of its arrows. A localization $L:A\to D$ at $W$ means that for every category $H$, precomposition with $L$ is fully faithful on functor categories and has essential image the functors $A\to H$ that send $W$ to isomorphisms. Enlarge universes if necessary. Let $P\subseteq A$ be a full subcategory, $i:P\to A$ its inclusion, $W_P=i^{-1}W$, $L_P:P\to D_P$ a localization at $W_P$, and $E:D_P\to D$ the induced functor, with comparison $E L_P\cong L i$. The inclusion is a left derivability structure if (a) every $X\in A$ admits an arrow $iP\to X$ in $W$, and (b) the following functor is final for every $X\in A$:
$$ (i\downarrow X)\longrightarrow(E\downarrow LX),\qquad(P,a:iP\to X)\longmapsto(L_PP,L(a)). $$
The comparison isomorphism is understood in this formula. Here $(i\downarrow X)$ has arrows $d:P\to P'$ satisfying $a'\circ i(d)=a$. Likewise $(E\downarrow LX)$ has objects $(Y,b:EY\to LX)$. Final means that for each $(Y,b)$ the category of triples $(P,a,c:Y\to L_PP)$ with $L(a)\circ E(c)=b$ is nonempty and connected; an arrow of triples is a $d:P\to P'$ satisfying both $a'\circ i(d)=a$ and $L_P(d)\circ c=c'$. Connected means any two objects are joined by a finite zigzag of arrows. This is equivalently the Guitart exactness of the inverse comparison square, together with existence of left resolutions. For an abelian category $C$, a standard example of the localization notion used here is $Q:K(C)\to D(C)$ at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; no assertion about a chosen subcategory being a derivability structure is implicit in this example.
